newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end mixed, corporate troubles haunt.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end mixed, corporate troubles haunt.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed mixed on Saturday on consolidation as investors, spooked over a string of corporate troubles, remained cautious and declined to be active participants, brokers said.
They expected the market to go through further consolidation early next week before a possible rebound.
The composite stock index stood at 732.32 at the close, down 1.32 points from Friday. Gainers edged out losers by 398 to 330 with 20.1 million shares changing hands in half-day trading.
"Investors lack confidence to jump into the market as corporate troubles linger on," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Taeil Media dropped 720 won to its new year low of 8,390 as rumours of impending debt default continued to spread in the market, brokers said.
The computer parts producer said Taeil had been facing temporary liquidity problems but it strongly denied the company would default.
Brokers said shares of troubled Jinro Group affiliates outperformed the market with Jinro Industries Co hitting its daily limit high of 4,840 won, up 350.
"Investors believe creditor banks' decisions were quite favourable," Choo said.

Creditor banks on Friday decided to extend principal payment to Jinro General Foods Co, Jinro Ltd, Jinro Construction Co and Jinro-Coors Brewing Co. They also agreed to supply funds to Jinro General Foods and Jinro Ltd.
Jinro Industries and Jinro Mass Merchandising would be sold to a third party, they said.

Brokers said banking shares were unaffected by a report by Moody's Investors Service on a possible downgrade review of ratings of Korea Exchange Bank, Korea First Bank, Commercial Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK.
Moody's said the action reflected the continued deterioration in the asset quality of the banks.
"It wasn't unexpected news," said Choo of Dongwon.
